title: How Client Funding Meets an Employee Purchase at the Micro Market Kiosk
content:
When an employee buys at the kiosk of an Unattended Micro Market Program market, the discount met from client funding is calculated from the subsidy model printed against the market format.

Two of the branches that clause once carried are **no longer in force**: the branch under which a model meeting a share of shelf price met the stated percentage of shelf price, and the branch under which a model meeting a flat amount met that flat amount once per shopping visit, have each been superseded by the current basis on which the share applied to a trip is settled. A model that meets nothing still meets nothing.

## The daily ceiling

Whatever the model yields is then held to the daily ceiling printed against the market format, measured as the total subsidy already drawn for that employee at that market on that day plus the subsidy this purchase would draw.

## Where funding has run out

Where no drawable funding remains on the agreement, no drawdown is posted, the employee pays the full shelf price, and the shortfall is reported to the client on the next settlement invoice rather than carried as a negative pool.

## Order of lots and matching

Drawdowns are taken from funding lots in order of the day the lot was funded, oldest lot first, and every drawdown row carries the employee till transaction that caused it so that a reversal can be matched back to the exact drawdown. A purchase reversed at the kiosk reverses its drawdown to the same funding lot it was taken from, and never to the newest lot.

## When subsidy may be drawn

Subsidy is only drawn while the agreement stands active or suspended, since a market that has not opened has rung no purchases and a closed market rings none. The standing and the funding standing on the agreement are read from the company's records before the drawdown is taken, not from the employee's account of the purchase.

superseded_clauses: a percent_discount model meets the stated percentage of shelf price
a fixed_per_visit model meets a flat amount once per shopping visit
